assumptions.text: All money is GBP in integer pence (minor units); no other currency exists for this library.

Enums closed from canvas decisions: pay-fee.method card|cash (fees decision 4), return-item.condition good|fair-wear|damaged (desk screen D4), inspect-item.outcome passed|failed, charge-card.response.outcome succeeded|declined (Stripe outcome as our adapter reports it).

Six messages (fee-balance, membership-current, item-returned, loan-overdue, item-failed-inspection, item-retired) stay inside the single deployable and get no wire contract; the code-level contract: and idempotent: tests in code.json cover them.
Ids are opaque strings: member numbers M-nnnn, asset tags, uuids for loans/reservations/attempts; formats are annotations only.
payLink is a path relative to the app origin, not an absolute URL, so notices survive a hostname change.

open_questions.text: pay-fee carries memberId, amountPence, method but no paymentAttemptId, yet the idempotency rule keys on it; should connect add paymentAttemptId to the payload (concern CC1)?
expire-reservations and lapse-memberships (clock commands) have no connect message and therefore no contract here (organise N2).

entries.name: Reserve Item
entries.description: A member asks lending to hold an available item for 48 hours; on success the item is reserved for them and nobody else can check it out.
semantics: One live reservation per (memberId, itemId); a repeat returns the existing hold
A hold lasts 48 calendar hours (define A10); a check-out against an expired hold is refused
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Check Out Item
entries.description: The desk volunteer asks lending to hand an item to a member; lending checks the borrow rule (membership current, balance zero, no overdue, fewer than three out) and, if allowed, opens a 14-day loan.
semantics: One open loan per itemId; a repeat for an item already out is rejected
Refused, with the failing reason, unless membership is current, balance is zero, no loan is overdue and fewer than three loans are open (lending decision 1)
The borrow rule is evaluated atomically with the check-out; two concurrent check-outs for a member's third item cannot both succeed
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Send Due Reminders
entries.description: The scheduler asks lending to send reminders for every loan due in two days or today; lending decides which loans and calls the email provider.
semantics: One notice per (loanId, reminderKind, date)
Re-running for the same asOfDate sends nothing new: one notice per (loanId, reminderKind, date)
entries.termsOfUse: The external party owns the wire contract; our adapter in the handling context translates. Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Send Due Notice
entries.description: Lending asks the email provider to tell a member their item is due; the provider owns the wire format, our adapter translates.
semantics: Provider de-duplicates on (loanId, dueOn, kind)
Provider de-duplicates on (loanId, dueOn, kind); a redelivery is harmless
entries.termsOfUse: The external party owns the wire contract; our adapter in the handling context translates. Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Return Item
entries.description: The desk volunteer records that a loan's item is back and in what condition; the loan closes, accrual stops, and a damaged condition queues an inspection.
semantics: A loan is returned once; a repeat is a no-op
A returned loan cannot be renewed, marked overdue or returned again
condition 'damaged' queues an inspection in inventory before the item is lent again
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Mark Loans Overdue
entries.description: The scheduler asks lending to mark every loan past its due date overdue as of the given date; each affected loan blocks further borrowing and starts accrual in fees.
semantics: A loan goes overdue once
Idempotent per asOfDate: a loan goes overdue once; a returned loan is never marked
entries.termsOfUse: The external party owns the wire contract; our adapter in the handling context translates. Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Accrue Late Fee
entries.description: The scheduler asks fees to add one day's late fee (GBP 1 per item, capped at replacement value) for every overdue loan as of the given date.
semantics: One accrual row per (loanId, date)
One accrual row per (loanId, date); accrual stops at the item's replacement value and at item-returned (fees decision 1)
entries.termsOfUse: The external party owns the wire contract; our adapter in the handling context translates. Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Send Fee Notice
entries.description: Fees asks the email provider to tell a member about a fee and give them a link to pay; the provider owns the wire format.
semantics: Provider de-duplicates on (memberId, feeId)
entries.termsOfUse: The external party owns the wire contract; our adapter in the handling context translates. Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Pay Fee
entries.description: A member (card, online) or the desk volunteer on their behalf (cash) pays against the balance; on success the balance falls and, if it reaches zero, borrowing is unblocked.
semantics: Client-supplied paymentAttemptId; a repeat returns the first outcome
A repeat with the same paymentAttemptId returns the first outcome and charges nothing (fees decision 3)
method cash makes no Stripe call and is recorded by the desk volunteer
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Charge Card
entries.description: Fees asks Stripe to charge a card for a fee amount; Stripe owns the API, our adapter sends currency, minor units and the attempt id as idempotency key and never sees card data (C1).
semantics: Stripe idempotency key = paymentAttemptId
Retry with the same idempotencyKey returns the original outcome; a later webhook with the same key changes nothing (CC1)
amountPence is GBP minor units; card data never crosses this boundary (C1)
entries.termsOfUse: Stripe owns the wire contract; changes land in fees' StripeGateway adapter (ACL) and never in the ledger model. Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Inspect Item
entries.description: The maintenance volunteer records an inspection outcome for an item; a failure takes the item out of lending and may lead to a damage charge.
semantics: outcome failed takes the item out of lending until repaired or retired (inventory decisions 1-2)
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Charge Damage Fee
entries.description: The coordinator adds a damage charge to a member's balance after a failed inspection; never above the item's replacement value.
semantics: Rejected when amountPence exceeds the item's replacement value (fees decision 2); only the coordinator may issue it
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

entries.name: Retire Item
entries.description: The maintenance volunteer retires an item; it leaves the catalogue view, keeps its history, and lending stops offering it.
semantics: A retired item is published to lending as item-retired and is never re-offered; its loan history is kept
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

plain_words.what: For every message that crosses a real boundary - a person to the app, the app to Stripe or the email provider, the scheduler to the app - we wrote down the exact fields, an example, who owns it and the rules the other side may rely on.
plain_words.decided: 13 contracts: 7 for screens people use, 6 inherited from outside systems (Stripe, email, the scheduler). 6 messages between modules inside the one program get no contract; tests cover them instead.
plain_words.assumed: All money is British pence as whole numbers, and the payment method is only card or cash.
plain_words.riskiest: pay-fee has no attempt id in its payload even though the no-double-charge rule depends on one; if that gap is not closed in connect, a retry can charge a card twice.
